title: Western Roman Empire
capsule: The Western Roman Empire denotes the Latin-speaking, Italy-based administrative half of the Roman Empire, formally separated from the eastern (Byzantine) half by the accession of Honorius and Arcadius following Theodosius I's death in 395 CE. Throughout the 5th century the western government at Ravenna — having abandoned Rome as a permanent capital under Honorius — struggled against Germanic federates: Visigoths sacked Rome in 410, Vandals in 455, and Hunnic pressure under Attila (d. 453) accelerated the dissolution of Rhine and Danubian frontiers. In 476 Odoacer deposed the last western emperor, the child Romulus Augustulus, and sent the imperial regalia to Constantinople, conventionally marking the western empire's end, though the eastern court recognized Julius Nepos as the legitimate emperor until his murder in 480. The dataset records the western polity from 395 to 475, consistent with the conventional 476 end date.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The administrative core of Italy, North Africa (until the Vandal conquest of 429–439), Gaul, and Hispania is documented by Roman administrative records, law codes, and extensive chronicle evidence; peripheral military control in Britain (abandoned c. 410) and along Rhine-Danube frontiers contracted rapidly in the 5th century, making the outer boundary increasingly nominal rather than effective administrative territory.
